Pairwise compatibility of the residues is equivalent to the sequence being induced by some integer \(n\pmod{\operatorname{lcm}(1,\dots,10)}\).

\[
\operatorname{lcm}(1,2,\dots,10)=2520
\]

Each \(n \pmod{2520}\) gives a distinct compatible sequence, so the number of valid sequences is \(2520\). The total number of possible sequences is:

\[
1\cdot 2\cdots 10=10!
\]

Thus

\[
p=\frac{2520}{10!}=\frac{2520}{3628800}=\frac{1}{1440}.
\]

So \(a=1\), \(b=1440\), and

\[
100a+b=100+1440=1540.
\]

\[
\boxed{1540}
\]
